model_annotation: This bar chart compares the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms generated by a base model, Mistralv0.2-Base, and its fine-tuned variants across six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis represents the negative log probability, scaled from -22 to -27, with lower values indicating higher probability (better performance). The horizontal axis lists the six specialties, each corresponding to a group of bars. Within each group, the first bar (light blue) represents the base model’s performance, while the subsequent bars (in shades of orange to dark brown) represent the performance of models fine-tuned on each of the six specialties, as indicated by the legend. For each specialty, the fine-tuned model on that specialty (e.g., the dark brown bar under "Cardio") consistently achieves the lowest negative log probability (highest probability), indicating superior performance. The base model (light blue) generally performs worse than all fine-tuned models, with its negative log probability values typically around -22 to -23. The fine-tuned models show varying performance across specialties, with the model fine-tuned on a given specialty performing best on that specialty’s terms. The bars are arranged in groups by specialty, and within each group, the bars are ordered from left to right as: base model, then fine-tuned models in the order: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning on a specific specialty improves performance on that specialty’s terminology, with the largest improvements observed in the fine-tuned model’s own domain.
